name: Skill proposer → genesis inbox
description: §3.3 of papers/research/em-wikiskill-absorption.md — the WikiSkill Proposer, composed from existing primitives. gather (core:exec) collects the knowledge-intervention ledger (skill-impact recent), the EM staged/quarantined pipeline, and the skills index; propose (agent:run, fs.read+fs.write only — NO shell, so it cannot run commands on the live shared tree) reads that context and writes ONE atomic proposal {action:create|patch|noop, target, patch, rationale, evidenceRefs} to data/skill-impact/proposals/<cid>.json; emit (core:exec) turns a non-noop proposal into a genesis INBOX card mechanically (no LLM in the card-write) and records a graduation intervention so the next proposer doesn't re-litigate it; notify reports back. NOTHING is auto-landed into skills/ — a human graduates the inbox card (§6.2, Kevin's confirmed default). Params: `agent` (who to notify), `cwd` (monorepo root for the proposer), optional `supervisor` (default http://localhost:39827). A `noop` outcome files no card and is a first-class honest result.

params.command: echo '=== IMPACT LEDGER (recent 40 interventions — read this FIRST) ==='; npx --no-install tsx dependencies/skill-impact/src/cli.ts recent 40 2>&1; echo; echo '=== EXPERIENCE-MEMORY PIPELINE (staged / quarantined) ==='; npx --no-install tsx packages/experience-memory/src/cli.ts yield 2>&1; echo; echo '=== SKILLS INDEX (name + trigger lines) ==='; grep -rn '^name:\|^when-to-use:' skills/ 2>/dev/null | head -160

params.prompt:
You are the colony's SKILL PROPOSER (WikiSkill Proposer, §3.3 of papers/research/em-wikiskill-absorption.md). Your job: read the knowledge-intervention ledger and the experience-memory pipeline, and propose AT MOST ONE atomic change to the skills/ library. You do NOT edit skills/ — you write a single proposal file that a human reviews in the genesis inbox and graduates or drops.

HARD RULES:
1. Bias hard toward NOOP. Only propose when the ledger shows a RECURRENT, GROUNDED pattern — e.g. a skill file churned repeatedly (multiple skill-edit records) with no consolidating change; a mutate-tip pattern that should become a durable skill; a cluster of em-verdicts pointing at a missing convention. If nothing is well-grounded in the evidence below, action="noop".
2. Ground EVERY non-noop proposal in SPECIFIC evidence from the ledger below — cite the actual intervention refs/targets or correction ids in evidenceRefs. No concrete evidence → noop. Do not invent a pattern to have something to say (read skills/fluency_is.md — manufactured confidence is the failure mode here).
3. Propose ONE thing. create = a new skill file; patch = a change to an existing one; noop = nothing worth a human's attention this round.
4. Do NOT re-propose something the ledger already shows as a `graduation` intervention (origin skill-propose:<target>) — that was already filed; re-litigating it is the exact waste this system exists to prevent.

OUTPUT: write EXACTLY ONE JSON object, and NOTHING else, to this exact path:
  data/skill-impact/proposals/{{run.correlationId}}.json
Shape:
  {
    "action": "create" | "patch" | "noop",
    "target": "skills/<name>.md"   (the file to create/patch; omit or "" for noop),
    "rationale": "why, in 2-4 sentences, tied to the evidence",
    "patch": "the proposed new content (create) or a concrete description of the change (patch); omit for noop",
    "evidenceRefs": ["skill-impact:<ref>", "corr:<id>", ...]
  }
Do NOT write to any other path. Do NOT edit any skill file. Write only that one JSON file. After writing it, reply with a one-line summary of what you proposed (or that you chose noop and why).

=== EVIDENCE (ledger + EM pipeline + skills index) ===
{{nodes.gather.result.stdout}}
